name: Lachlan Giles Body Lock Passing System
description: The Body Lock Pass by Lachlan Giles covers no-gi entries, pinning, knee clearance and finishes, with counters, closed-guard opening and narrated rolling.
summary: A dedicated no-gi body-lock course covering the entire pass, from establishing the lock to clearing the legs, with narrated sparring.
overview:
The Body Lock Pass by Lachlan Giles follows one passing family in depth across six volumes. It covers entering the body lock, pinning the opponent, clearing the knee line and finishing, alongside responses to counters and defenses.

The course also includes the Sao Paulo closed-guard break and narrated rolling. That combination suits passers who want both the mechanics of the body lock and examples of its use in sparring, rather than a collection of unrelated passes.

related_content.name: Gordon Ryan Passing System
related_content.relationship: For wider coverage of split squat, half butterfly, knee shields and passing from leg entanglements, alongside body-lock material.

flashcards.question: Why does connecting the hands in the public Lachlan Giles body-lock explanation not yet complete the pass?
flashcards.answer: The written explanation still has the passer clear the first knee and then free the remaining leg. Securing the torso connection and clearing the legs are separate events.

flashcards.question: In the public explanation of Lachlan Giles’s body-lock pass, why distinguish the first knee clearance from the final leg clearance?
flashcards.answer: After the first knee clears, the description still accounts for the other leg being held in half guard. Clearing one knee therefore does not establish that both legs are free.
flashcards.answer_line: One leg may remain in half guard

products.title: The Body Lock Pass
products.blurb: Six volumes devoted to body-lock passing, with counters, closed-guard opening and narrated rolling.
products.best_for: No-gi passers looking for depth in one close-contact passing family.

fits: You want to make body-lock passing a substantial part of your no-gi game.
You can secure the lock but struggle to clear the legs or finish the pass.

includes: Body-lock entries, pinning, knee clearance, finishes and responses to counters.
Sao Paulo closed-guard opening within the body-lock approach.
Narrated rolling accompanying the technical instruction.
limits: The six volumes concentrate on the body lock; they are not a broad survey of outside passing and open-guard passing styles.
